Hi Ben — thanks again for the sync earlier. I'm taking over the technical handoff from the sales team and want to make the kickoff as friction-free as possible. Attaching a short checklist and a bundle of SDK samples to help your engineers stand up the integration in a staging environment this week.

High-level asks for our kickoff:
- Confirm a 60–90 minute technical kickoff this week (we have openings Tue/Wed morning PT).
- Share the primary contact(s) on your side for SDK/PT testing and procurement (if there are billing/contract questions).
- Flag any strict network egress/firewall constraints (IPs or proxy).

What I'm attaching: clearline-onboard-checklist.pdf (one-pager), redwood-sdk-samples-v1.3.zip (node/python examples), migration-window-slots.xlsx.

Below is a short migration/implementation plan so your team can review before kickoff. More details and code snippets are in the SDK samples zip.

Planned flow
1) Sandbox onboarding (day 0–2): get API key, configure SDK, run sample inference calls to staging endpoints.
2) Validation (day 2–4): run load tests (we provide a harness), verify latency/throughput, and validate token accounting.
3) Cutover (scheduled window): migrate traffic to production endpoint with a staged ramp (10%/50%/100%) over agreed windows.

Key technical notes (abridged):
- SDK versions: use redwood-sdk v1.3.x (samples included).
- Recommended client timeouts: connect=3s, read=60s for generation calls.
- Retry/backoff: use exponential backoff with jitter; start with base 250ms, max 10s, cap retries to 6 for idempotent calls.
- Rate limits: include token-budget headers; if you see 429s, back off to client-side queue with token-bucket smoothing.

Can you confirm the kickoff time and the name/email of your primary engineer so we can send a calendar invite?

Thanks,
Vivek

Perfect — Wed 21 Sep 10:00 PT is confirmed. Calendar invite sent. Emilie and you are great points of contact.

Below are the implementation-ready details Emilie can hand to the infra team. I'll also post these in the Kickoff notes doc but wanted to surface them here for quick review.

1) SDK setup (v1.3.x) - Node example (excerpt):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'us' });

// simple generation call
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: 'Summarize user logs' });

Python example (excerpt):
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'], region='us')
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-small', prompt='Summarize user logs')

2) Endpoint migration strategy
- Dual-write/dual-read coexistence: route 10% of requests to Redwood prod endpoint and 90% to existing vendor for 48–72 hours. Compare token usage, latencies, and quality metrics.
- Traffic ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over windows of 4–8 hours depending on SLA tolerance.
- Fallthrough policy: if Redwood returns 5xx or timeout > configured read timeout, automatically failback to prior provider for that request.

3) Retries & timeouts (recommended defaults)
- Connect timeout: 3000ms
- Read timeout: 60000ms for generation; 15000ms for embeddings
- Retries: only for idempotent calls (embeddings, status checks). For generation, implement safe retry semantics (check request-id or dedupe at server side).
- Backoff: exponential with full jitter; base=250ms, factor=2, max=10000ms, max-retries=6.

4) Rate limit handling
- Redwood responds with headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Honor Remaining and reduce concurrency proactively when Remaining < 20% of Limit.
- Implement token-bucket client-side to smooth bursts.
- If you receive 429: immediate short backoff (randomized 500–1500ms), then exponential backoff as above; surface aggregate 429s to monitoring and trigger ops paging if >5% of requests are 429 in a 5-minute window.

5) Observability/telemetry
- Include a request-id header (X-Request-Id) on all calls to help tracing.
- Send sample payloads and a small synthetic traffic run before the migration window so we can validate metrics in the console.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-samples-v1.3.zip contains runnable examples, a Postman collection, and a small load-test harness.

If Emilie can share a short network diagram or proxy egress details before kickoff, Aditya will review and suggest the minimal firewall changes.

Thanks — see you Wed.
Vivek

Quick technical notes from infra (straight to the engineers):
- Connection pooling: prefer HTTP/2 with multiplexing for generation calls to reduce connection churn; set max concurrent streams per connection to 50.
- TLS: we support mutual TLS if you need stricter egress controls — let us know and we can provide cert signing instructions.
- Backoff nuance: when you get partial failures (stream cut/partial chunk), do NOT blindly retry the same prompt; instead, mark as partial and re-run with a dedup token to avoid double-charging.
- Latency knobs: trim max tokens and set top_k/top_p appropriately; large model responses can hit the read timeout if not bounded.
- Proxy behavior: if your proxy rewrites headers, ensure X-Request-Id and our X-RateLimit-* headers are preserved for accurate client-side throttling.

If you want, I can be on the call for the first 20 minutes to walk through the HTTP flow and header expectations.

-Aditya
